project.name: libcoap
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace checkout at `/src/libcoap` is on commit `0d6c7d686b1bc8eb48ee6a5fbd0f9edf1ef6b8ab`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. All line anchors below were resolved against that staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the unfixed `coap_split_uri_sub()` entry guard shown in `patch.diff`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 48362 (libcoap): AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in `coap_split_uri_sub`, reached from `coap_get_uri_path`.
bug_description.normalized: In the staged libcoap checkout `0d6c7d686b1bc8eb48ee6a5fbd0f9edf1ef6b8ab`, the exact staged 260-byte witness is copied into a heap-backed `coap_pdu_t` and parsed as a UDP CoAP message with token length 0. The copied 256-byte option/body region ends with a lone option header byte `0x30`; under libcoap's option encoding that final byte contributes delta 3 and length 0, so the cumulative option number becomes 35 (`Proxy-Uri`) with no value bytes. `coap_pdu_parse_opt_base()` rejects that length and `coap_pdu_parse()` returns failure, but the fuzz target ignores the return value and still calls `coap_get_uri_path()` on the populated PDU. `coap_check_option()` re-finds the malformed `Proxy-Uri`, `coap_split_proxy_uri()` forwards `coap_opt_value(q)` at the end of the copied PDU body together with `coap_opt_length(q) == 0`, and `coap_split_uri_sub()` dereferences `*p` before checking `len`. AddressSanitizer therefore reports a `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/uri.c:72` in `coap_split_uri_sub`. The fix matches this exact obligation by changing the entry guard to `if (!str_var || !uri || len == 0)`.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled UDP packet into the heap-backed PDU buffer and records the post-header extent later re-parsed as options.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is a 260-byte file. Its first four bytes are UDP CoAP header `70 ff bd bd`, so the copied post-header body is 256 bytes long; that body ends with the final option header byte `0x30` that later becomes the zero-length `Proxy-Uri`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The copied bytes are first interpreted as the vulnerability-relevant semantic state here: the trailing header `0x30` becomes option number 35 (`Proxy-Uri`) with explicit `len == 0`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the exact 256-byte copied option stream, the earlier option deltas accumulate to option 32 before the last byte. The final byte `0x30` therefore contributes delta 3 and length 0, yielding `COAP_OPTION_PROXY_URI` with no value bytes.
tainted_value_origin.note: This zero-length option state is what later crosses the API boundary into `coap_split_uri_sub()`.

root_cause.description: Missing empty-input guard. `coap_split_uri_sub()` only rejects null pointers and continues when `len == 0`; the patch adds `|| len == 0` at this exact check.
root_cause.note: With step 7, `str_var` points to the end of the copied PDU body and `len == 0`, so the fixed guard would have returned before any dereference.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The first scheme/path probe dereferences the empty `Proxy-Uri` value pointer one byte past the heap-backed PDU body.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/uri.c:72:7` in `coap_split_uri_sub`, with stack `coap_split_uri_sub -> coap_split_proxy_uri -> coap_get_uri_path`.

parser_admitted.description: After the copied header `70 ff bd bd` is accepted as CoAP version 1, `token_length == 0` makes option parsing start at the first byte of the 256-byte copied body.
parser_admitted.note: The header parse does not reject this witness: `hdr[0] >> 6` is version 1, `pdu->token_length = 0`, and `pdu->code = 0xff`, so the options loop is entered.

fine_trace.note: Source. This copies the exact 260-byte witness into the heap-backed PDU and records a 256-byte post-header body. The copied body's last byte is the option header `0x30` that later becomes the zero-length `Proxy-Uri`.

The copied header bytes `70 ff` make this a non-empty CoAP packet with `token_length == 0` and `code == 0xff`. Option parsing therefore starts at the first byte of the 256-byte copied body rather than after a token.

When the loop reaches the final copied body byte `0x30`, that one-byte option header contributes delta 3 and length 0. The earlier option headers have already accumulated current option number 32, so this iteration materializes option 35 (`Proxy-Uri`) with `len == 0`.

fine_trace.code: case COAP_OPTION_PROXY_URI:     if (len < 1 || len > 1034) res = 0; break;
fine_trace.note: Because step 3 produced `pdu->max_opt == 35` and `len == 0`, the `COAP_OPTION_PROXY_URI` length check fails. `coap_pdu_parse_opt()` sets `good = 0`, so `coap_pdu_parse()` returns failure, but the malformed option bytes remain stored in the PDU.
The fuzz target ignores the boolean return from `coap_pdu_parse()`. Even after step 4 marks the packet invalid, the same populated `pdu` is still passed into `coap_get_uri_path()`.

Re-iterating the malformed PDU returns a non-null `q` for option 35 (`Proxy-Uri`). `coap_check_option()` / `coap_option_next()` only structurally parse options and match filtered numbers; they do not re-apply `coap_pdu_parse_opt_base()`'s `len >= 1` restriction.

For the one-byte option header `0x30`, `coap_opt_length(q) == 0` and `coap_opt_value(q) == q + 1 == pdu->token + 256`, the first byte past the copied message body. `coap_get_uri_path()` forwards that exact end-of-buffer pointer and explicit zero length into `coap_split_proxy_uri()`.

Root cause. The entry guard only rejects null pointers. With step 7, `str_var` is a non-null pointer at the end of the copied PDU body and `len == 0`, so the missing `|| len == 0` term added by the patch is the only check that would stop the dereference path.

Sink. After `p = str_var`, line 72 immediately reads `*p` even though step 8 admitted `len == 0`. Because step 7 passed the end-of-body pointer `pdu->token + 256`, this dereference lands 0 bytes to the right of the 262-byte heap allocation reported by ASan.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of the 262-byte region `[0x612000000040, 0x612000000146)`. In this staged tree, `coap_pdu_init()` allocates `min(size, 256) + pdu->max_hdr_size = 256 + 6 = 262` bytes for the 260-byte witness.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The patch changes the entry guard to `if (!str_var || !uri || len == 0) return -1;`, so the zero-length `Proxy-Uri` forwarded in steps 6-7 is rejected before line 72 evaluates `*p`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_48362 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` file to `/out/pdu_parse_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `coap_split_uri_sub` with stack `coap_split_uri_sub -> coap_split_proxy_uri -> coap_get_uri_path`.

format.name: 260-byte UDP CoAP packet witness
format.contract: Exact staged 260-byte file `poc`. Its first four bytes are UDP CoAP header `70 ff bd bd`, so `token_length == 0`, and its 256-byte post-header option region ends with a final option header byte `0x30`. For this exact layout, the preceding option deltas accumulate to option 32, so that last byte becomes option 35 (`Proxy-Uri`) with `len == 0`; `coap_get_uri_path()` then forwards `coap_opt_value(q)` at the end of the copied PDU body into `coap_split_uri_sub()`.
